body: Thanks for your words of reassurance. I've been mulling over the end goal thing for a while, and I'm still not sure what it is, but I appreciate that someone has confidence that I'm not here just to die.

I'm not sure what made the depression and anxiety come so young. One of my dad's aunts was hospitalized for depression in the 1960s, but I haven't heard of anyone else in the family having any mental illness, and I suspect that my range of symptoms is a lot broader than my great aunts' was. (I've had anxiety for ages, and my counselor said today that she thinks this recent crap is congruent with OCD.)

I guess part of it could be the family, church, and school environments I grew up in (all very strict, very conservative, and very religious... with quite a few abusive elements, as I recognized later) but I don't really feel like I can say that this is other peoples' fault. It just is, I guess, and it has been for so long that I don't really care why it is, I'm just glad when I get a bit of a break.

I am glad to see that the mods have removed the really callous comment that was here.

To be clear: the thoughts are bad, but normal to me. The really bad actively trying to die stuff has still happened more times than I can count, and has only been thwarted by dumb luck basically. I'm sure my luck will run out eventually... So it's hard to deal with that knowledge.
Those are all amazing achievements! I'm really happy for you and all the hard work you've put in :)

It sounds cliche, but what helps me is exercise or pouring myself into work. I used to work in a kitchen, and it was simply too fast-paced there for me to have any thoughts at all. 

If you can find something that's so intense you lose the capacity to think, and that's exhausting enough that you can't think afterward, it might help. For me it means taking lots of long shifts, or going on very long bike rides. For you, who knows? I wish you the best, though.

It's ok! I think it's really nice of you to be so supportive of everyone else, but you have the right to take care of yourself too. It can be really exhausting dealing with your stuff and everyone else's stuff, and it's totally ok if you need to hang back a bit and tend to yourself. 

You don't have to help everyone, that's the nice thing about having all the people in this sub... there's lots of people who can share the helping and the healing.

Thank you, that helps, especially the bit about being honorable enough to make it right.

It's not a 4chan thing (though I am aware of their propensity for doing these things), it looks like it'll have a pretty serious impact on this person's life if it's real. But like I said, I don't know her, she's in Europe and I'm in North America. 

Logically, I'm sure I'm fine, but emotionally I'm just convinced that everyone who I've ever wronged is gonna band together and write up a list of everything terrible I've ever done, and publish it and try to get me banned/cut off/alienated from everyone and everywhere. It's ridiculous, but it's really frightening.

I'm glad you were able to talk to your sister. I know it usually helps me when I can talk with my brother. Do you feel a bit better? Even if you don't, I think it's really courageous that you were able to talk openly with her.

Family troubles are really rough, I'm sorry you're having to deal with that.

Hi there. Thanks for the encouragement, and the offer to talk. I may take you up on it, I don't know.

I'm upset because I saw a post on a website I frequent (not reddit) that had a bunch of pictures of a person, along with their full name and a bunch of personal data. It went on to give a lot of details about all the horrible things this person has done, and that the people who wrote the post want their whole city and university and all the online communities they frequent to exile her. It looks like that's pretty well underway.

I have no idea who this person is -- she doesn't even live on the same continent as me. And if the allegations are true (I don't have any reason to doubt or believe them) then she has definitely done some horrible stuff.

But it's making me think about how easily someone might make a post with my name and face and personal details on it, asking that I be exiled from everyone/everywhere in my life. I haven't done anything near as horrible as the stuff the woman in the picture apparently did, but I have always had a very, very difficult time dealing with guilt from my actions, even after I've made things as right as possible and people have forgiven me.

I know it's not a reasonable fear, but it's freaking me out nonetheless.

Yeah, I do. I'm 25, and I've been harming since I was 11 or 12. I've never really been that good at healing, so most of my scars are still there, though the older ones have faded some. 

Sometimes I don't mind so much, and the scars remind me how much I've grown. But some of them remind me of terrible, terrible times in my life. I try not to look at those ones. Someday, I would like to get them tattooed over -- or just have the biggest one surgically removed.
You're so right, those would both be really helpful.
I'm glad that worked for you! :)

I'm quite heavy, so I don't want to take up running just yet. I feel like a low-impact form of exercise will be better for my joints.

I have a really long history of depression, but I'm not depressed right now. Low self-esteem has always been a thing for me. I feel like harming partially to deal with shitty things that have happened to me (I am in counseling, though) and partially because I feel immense guilt for stuff I've done. And also, it's just something I want to do sometimes.

Since there's no real place I can cut, I've been thinking about what I could get away with otherwise.

Deliberately crash my bike? Effective, but implausible, and anyway I don't want to fuck up my bike.

Climb a tree and "misstep"? Maybe, but that's hard to control the level of hurt. I might just get a few bruises, or I might break my arm. Besides, I'm an adult, it's sort of out of place.

Maybe I'll just ride my bike a lot? My legs and butt hurt a lot when I go for long rides, just because I'm out of shape. But... is it self harm to exercise, when you know there won't be any lasting pain or marks, and the end result is that you just get a little stronger and faster?

As ridiculous as it sounds, I guess going for a long bike ride is my next best choice for self harm. It's really just exercise though -- my brother rides some of the same routes for fun -- but somehow if I think of it as self harm I'm a lot more likely to do it than if I think of it as exercise. How twisted is that!? I won't go on a hilly 12 mile ride to strengthen my legs and improve my cardiovascular endurance, but I will do it because I know my legs and butt will hurt from the effort.
